description: Opdrachtgever heeft als doel om op basis van deze Europese openbare aanbestedingsprocedure volgens de Aanbestedingswet 2012 te komen tot een raamovereenkomst met 3 (drie) Opdrachtnemers, waarbij de afdeling Communicatie en Kabinetszaken, van Opdrachtgever, haar afzonderlijke (deel)opdrachten aan de gecontracteerde Opdrachtnemers kan verstrekken zonder daar afzonderlijke aanbestedingsprocedures voor te moeten doorlopen. Deze opdracht bestaat uit het leveren van inhuur professionals Communicatie & Kabinetszaken en betreft een raamovereenkomst met een geraamde waarde van €2.140.000,-. Het genoemde bedrag is een indicatie, derhalve kan aan het genoemde bedrag geen rechten ontleend worden. De opdrachtwaarde over de totale looptijd van de raamovereenkomst wordt gemaximeerd op 150% van het bedrag zoals hierboven vermeld bij ‘Omvang opdracht’. Dit leidt tot een maximale opdrachtwaarde excl. btw van deze aanbesteding van €3.210.000,-. Als deze waarde bereikt is mag er alleen nog volgens de bepalingen van de artikelen 2.163a t/m 2.163g van de Aanbestedingswet 2012 gebruik gemaakt worden van de raamovereenkomst. Als op deze bepalingen geen beroep meer kan worden gedaan, sorteert de raamovereenkomst geen effect meer en mag er door de gemeente geen gebruik meer van worden gemaakt, ongeacht de dan nog resterende looptijd van de raamovereenkomst. De raamovereenkomst zal in dat geval – als de maximale waarde is bereikt of deze zeer binnenkort zal worden overschreden - door de gemeente met de Opdrachtnemer worden opgezegd met een opzeggingstermijn van één maand. Door deze opzegging ontstaat geen recht op schadevergoeding van de gemeente aan de Opdrachtnemer.

description: Dinamikus beszerzési rendszer létrehozása „K26123 Fémcsövek, idomok és karimák beszerzése közszolgáltatáshoz” tárgyban 36 hónap időtartamra, tervezetten nettó 190 000 000, HUF keretösszeg erejéig. A dinamikus beszerzési rendszer keretében különböző típusú és méretű fémcsövek és hozzá tartozó idomok, illetve karimák szállítása és adásvétele kerül megvalósításra. Ajánlatkérő távhőszolgáltatási területén üzemelő, közszolgáltatást ellátó távhőtechnológiai létesítményeinek felújítási és karbantartási munkái során különböző típusú és méretű fémcsövek és hozzá tartozó idomok, illetve karimák kerülnek felhasználásra. A fémcsöveket és idomokat, valamint karimákat az alábbi termék kategóriákban kívánjuk beszerezni: 1. kategória: Hegeszthető acélcsövek Jellemzően, de nem kizárólagosan EN 10216-2 szabvány szerinti varrat nélküli acélcső, EN 10217-2 szabvány szerinti hosszvarratos vagy spirálvarratos acélcső, EN 10217-5 szabvány szerinti, spirálvarrattal hegesztett acélcső. 2. kategória: Hegeszthető acél idomok Jellemzően, de nem kizárólagosan: könyök idom (forrcsőív), T-idom, koncentrikus szűkítő idom, excentrikus szűkítő idom, mélydomború edényfenék, hegeszthető fekete karmantyú. 3. kategória: Karimák Jellemzően, de nem kizárólagosan: hegtoldatos karima PN 6, DIN 2631 és MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint; hegtoldatos karima PN 16, DIN 2633 és MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint; hegtoldatos karima PN 25, DIN 2634 és MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint; hegtoldatos karima PN 40, DIN 2635 és MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint; vakkarima PN16, PN25, PN40 nyomásfokozatban, MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint; horganyzott menetes karima PN 10-16, MSZ EN 1092-1 szabvány szerint. 4. kategória: Menetes idomok Jellemzően, de nem kizárólagosan: horganyzott menetes idomok, sárgaréz és/vagy vörös öntvény idomok MSZ EN ISO 228-1 szabvány szerinti menet kialakításban, rozsdamentes acél menetes idomok. Ajánlatkérőnél az üzemeltetés során felmerülő, konkrét igénye alapján, tervezetten kategóriánként a mennyiség a teljes időszakra vonatkozóan (36 hónap): 1. kategória: Hegeszthető acélcsövek 83 490 kg. 2. kategória: Hegeszthető acél idomok 29 272 db. 3. kategória: Karimák 8 154 db. 4. kategória: Menetes idomok 28 513 db. A megadott mennyiség a korábbi felhasználási tapasztalatok alapján került meghatározásra, ún. tapasztalati mennyiség, a beszerzett mennyiség ezen tapasztalati adattól eltérhet. DBR keretében odaítélendő egyes szerződések várható maximális mennyisége: 1. kategória: Hegeszthető acélcsövek 11 000 kg. 2. kategória: Hegeszthető acél idomok 3 500 db. 3. kategória: Karimák 820 db. 4. kategória: Menetes idomok 3 020 db. A DBR-ben megvalósítandó konkrét közbeszerzésre vonatkozó pontos, részletes műszaki leírást és szerződésestervezetet ajánlatkérő az ajánlattételi felhívás megküldésével egyidejűleg bocsátja rendelkezésre. Ajánlatkérő az eljárás jelen szakaszában a beszerzendő termékek általános műszaki elvárásait tartalmazó műszaki leírást és szerződéses feltételeket bocsátja a részvételre jelentkezők számára, amelyek az egyes termékkategóriák vonatkozásában tartalmazzák az általános elvárásokat. Ajánlatkérő fenntartja annak a lehetőségét, hogy a beszerzendő termékek beazonosítása, valamint a termékekkel szemben támasztott műszaki elvárások teljesíthetősége érdekében az ajánlattételi szakaszokban referencia termékeket nevezzen meg. Ajánlatkérő a Kbt. 107. § (2) bekezdése alapján fenntartja annak a lehetőségét, hogy a DBR-ben megvalósítandó konkrét közbeszerzések során - a konkrét közbeszerzések tárgyától és jellegétől függően - részajánlat-tételi lehetőséget határozzon meg az ajánlattételi felhívásban az abban foglalt konkrét beszerzési igényre vonatkozóan. Ajánlatkérő fenntartja a jogot, hogy a DBR-ben megvalósítandó konkrét közbeszerzés(ek) eredményeként akár egyedi adásvételi szerződést, akár egyedi adásvételi keretszerződést kössön. Ajánlatkérő amennyiben keretszerződést köt és keretösszeg kerül meghatározásra, úgy 70%-os ajánlatkérői lehívási kötelezettséggel, és emellett a szerződés tárgyát képező egyes termékek beszerzésimennyisége kizárólag tájékoztató jellegű becsült mennyiséggel, amelytől Ajánlatkérő jogosult eltérni. A 321/2015. (X. 30.) Korm. rendelet 46.§ (3) bekezdés: bármely meghatározott gyártmányú, eredetű, típusú dologra, eljárásra, tevékenységre, személyre, szabadalomra vagy védjegyre való hivatkozás, megnevezés csak a tárgy jellegének egyértelmű meghatározása érdekében történik, a megnevezés mellett a „vagy azzal egyenértékű” minden esetben értendő. Egyenértékű termék megajánlása esetén az egyenértékűséget ajánlattevőnek az ajánlatában igazolnia kell. III.4.1) Alkalmassági követelmény(ek)/Hivatkozások meghatározott szállításokra (BT-750 mező) szakasz folytatása: Ajánlatkérő a 321/2015. (X. 30.) Korm. rendelet 21/A. §-ában előírtakon túl további szerződésszegési köröket, amellyel érintett teljesítések igazolását elfogadja, nem ír elő. Ajánlatkérő a 321/2015. Korm. rendelet 21/A. § alapján elfogadja az alkalmasság alátámasztására azon referenciákat is, amelyek esetén bár szerződésszegés történt, de a gazdasági szereplő szerződésszegésért való felelőssége – a szerződést kötő másik fél által nem vitatottan – nem áll fenn. A Kbt. 65. § (6) bekezdése alapján a fenti követelményeknek a közös ajánlattevők együttesen is megfelelhetnek. A Kbt. 107. § (8a) bekezdése alapján amennyiben az alkalmassági követelmények tekintetében változás áll be a DBR-be felvett érvényes részvételi jelentkezést benyújtó gazdasági szereplő, annak kapacitást nyújtó szervezete vagy alvállalkozója esetében, azt a gazdasági szereplő köteles haladéktalanul jelezni Ajánlatkérőnek. A Kbt. 107. § (8b) bekezdése alapján azon részvételre jelentkezők esetében, akik jelentkezésüket a részvételi határidő lejártát követően nyújtják be, a jelen pontban rögzített időszak meghatározásához használt referenciaidőpont alatt a felhívás feladása helyett a részvételi jelentkezés benyújtása értendő.

title: Germany – Contractor's all-risk insurance services – Projektversicherung GSH HLK Hagen-Hamm
description: Die DB InfraGO plant die Generalsanierung des Hochleistungskorridors Hagen-Hamm. Die Investitionssumme für dieses Projekt wird mit ca. EUR 855 Mio. veranschlagt. Hiervon sind bereits ca. EUR 45 Mio. über einen bestehenden Vertrag abgerechnet worden. Der hier neu ausgeschriebene Versicherungsvertrag wird den bestehenden Vertrag ablösen. Es wird mit einer derzeit geplanten Bauzeit bis zum 31.12.2028 gerechnet. Der Versicherungsvertrag beginnt nach Beendigung des Ausschreibungsverfahrens mit dem Datum des Zuschlages im Anschluss an eine derzeit bestehende Vorlaufdeckung. (Typ M) In der Haftpflichtversicherung beträgt die Deckungssumme je Schadenfall EUR 25.000.000 pauschal für Personen-, Sach- und Vermögensschäden, einschließlich der Leistungen aus der Umwelthaftpflichtversicherung. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung steht eine separate Deckungssumme je Schadenfall von EUR 10.000.000 pauschal für Sach- und Vermögensschäden zur Verfügung. Die vorgenannten Summen sind dreifach maximiert. Die Extendend Maintenance im Teil Bauleistungs- und Montageversicherung beträgt 42 Monate. Die Nachhaftung beträgt in der Haftpflichtversicherung 10 Jahre, in der Umwelthaftpflicht- und Umweltschadenversicherung 5 Jahre. Der generelle Selbstbehalt beträgt mindestens EUR 25.000. Für Personenschäden entfällt der Selbstbehalt. In der Planungshaftpflichtversicherung ist die erweiterte Planungsdeckung eingeschlossen. Im Rahmen der erweiterten Planungsdeckung beträgt der Selbstbehalt EUR 100.000

title: Ireland – Feasibility study, advisory service, analysis – Provision of Multidisciplinary Consultancy Services for the Development of the Tuam Creative Technologies Hub
description: Action Tuam CLG invites tenders from suitably qualified and experienced multidisciplinary consultancy teams for the provision of professional services to support the feasibility assessment, business planning and development of the proposed Tuam Creative Technologies Hub in Tuam, County Galway. The appointment will involve an integrated programme of consultancy services encompassing strategic and business case development, market and stakeholder engagement, academic and research opportunities, comparative site assessment, technical and infrastructure considerations, financial modelling, governance, funding strategy and project development planning. The successful consultant will be required to undertake a comparative desk-based assessment of three potential sites, followed by a more detailed evaluation of one site selected by Action Tuam. The assignment will also include stakeholder and community engagement, development of promotional and marketing materials, and preparation of the reports, recommendations and supporting evidence required to inform subsequent investment and implementation decisions. The project is supported through Enterprise Ireland's Smart Regions Enterprise Innovation Scheme, Stream 4 (Feasibility and Priming). The consultancy will be delivered on a fixed-fee basis, with defined deliverables, milestones and reporting requirements. Full details of the required services, deliverables, tender submission requirements and evaluation methodology are provided in the accompanying procurement documentation. All communications and requests for clarification concerning this competition must be submitted through the eTenders messaging facility.

description: The HSE wishes to invite tenders from suitable suppliers to undertake an external evaluation of Ushers Island Health and Addiction Care Facility (HACF), operated by Dublin Simon and funded by HSE and Department of Health (DoH). Ushers Island delivers a suite of integrated, low threshold health, addiction and recovery services for people experiencing homelessness and severe social exclusion. The service model operates across a continuum that includes Blood Borne Virus (BBV) treatment, Detoxification, Step Up Step Down (SUSD) Medical care, Stabilisation, and Recovery Phase 1. Services are designed to respond flexibly to fluctuating clinical needs, support hospital avoidance, and discharge, and promote sustained engagement for individuals with complex physical health, mental health, substance use and social care needs.

title: Framework for the provison of Temporary & Interim Staff Services
description: Scottish Procurement is seeking to procure the fifth generation of the Temporary and Interim Staff Services Framework. title: Supply and Support of Integrated Workplace Management System
description: North Ayrshire Council (NAC) is seeking to procure a cloud-hosted Integrated Workplace Management System (IWMS) to replace its existing Computer Aided Facilities Management (CAFM) solution. The new solution will provide a single, integrated platform to support the management of the Council's operational property portfolio, encompassing asset management, maintenance management, statutory compliance, financial monitoring, reporting and governance.

title: 26055 Child Weight Management
description: Since 2023, there has been a standalone, integrated Child Weight Management Service in Cambridgeshire, commissioned by Public Health. As the service is soon coming to an end, we intend to go out to procurement for a successive Child Weight Management Service across Cambridgeshire. The new service will be a 3 step (tier) integrated service, combining universal preventative support with more targeted group and one to one programmes. The service will be delivered both face to face and online across the county, with a proportionate universalism approach used to address key obesity related health inequalities.

description: Canada is seeking offers from Offerors to provide wireless internal communications systems for use onboard Canadian Coast Guard (CCG) vessels located across Canada. It is expected that PSPC will issue one Standing Offer as a result of this Request For Standing Offer. The standing offer will be available for use by CCG users across Canada. title: Správa webu mcvrk.mzk.cz
description: Předmětem zakázky je správa webového portálu mcvrk.mzk.cz, která konkrétně představuje: - Servisní podporu – udržování webového portálu v provozu. Zejména je třeba řešit chyby a výpadky tak, aby web byl provozuschopný, schopný plnit svůj účel a jeho zabezpečení odpovídalo obecně známému stavu technických znalostí a dále je třeba odstraňovat incidenty spojené s provozem webu. - Služby rozvoje webu – úprava stávajících funkcí webu, vytváření nových funkcionalit webu a vytváření jakýchkoli jiných změn nebo doplnění webu včetně udělení oprávnění k užití. Bližší informace v přiložené Výzvě k podání nabídky.

title: Oprava elektroinstalací – rámcová smlouva
description: Předmětem veřejné zakázky „Oprava elektroinstalací – rámcová smlouva“ je uzavření rámcové smlouvy o dílo na provádění průběžných oprav, úprav, dodávek a montáží elektroinstalací v objektech zadavatele podle jeho aktuálních provozních potřeb, a to s jedním dodavatelem. Podrobné požadavky zadavatele jsou uvedeny v přílohách výzvy k podání nabídek. Předmětem jsou zejména elektroinstalační, montážní, opravné a související stavebně-technické práce a související dodávky materiálu, měření, zkoušky a revize. Předpokládaná hodnota ve výši 4.000.000,- Kč bez DPH je maximální nepřekročitelnou hodnotou rámcové smlouvy. Jedná se o celkový maximální finanční limit rámcové smlouvy; zadavatel není povinen tento limit vyčerpat.

title: Leirikeskuskuljetukset, Kuopion evankelisluterilainen seurakuntayhtymä
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat henkilökuljetukset linja-autoilla Kuopion evankelis-luterilaisen srk-yhtymän leirikeskuskuljetuksiin Poukamaan ja Rytkylle tarjouspyyntöasiakirjojen mukaisesti. Hankinta on jaettu neljään (4) osa-alueeseen. Tarjoaja voi tarjota yhteen tai useampaan osa-alueeseen. Toimittajiksi valitaan yksi (1) toimittaja per osa-alue. title: RFSO - Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services in Yukon (Up to 5)
description: This requirement is for the Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC). The Department of Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada (CIRNAC), Yukon Region is responsible for managing multiple contaminated sites in Yukon, including Type II abandoned mine sites. In order to meet CIRNAC’s project objectives, CIRNAC requires Hydrotechnical and Geotechnical Services to support ongoing care and maintenance, and advance remediation plans at multiple Type II mine sites and other DTA sites in the Yukon region. These sites have a variety of different geotechnical and hydrotechnical challenges associated with them. The specific scopes for supplying services to each site will vary according to each site’s needs. Works for each of these sites will be issued on an as-and-when requested basis, detailed in each call-up. The work under these SOAs is intended to be consistent with CIRNAC’s Contaminated Sites Management Policy whose objectives include: 1) to meet federal and departmental policy requirements and legal obligations regarding the management of contaminated sites; 2) to require that, where a suspected contaminated site has been identified, the site be assessed in a timely, consistent and cost effective manner; 3) to provide a scientifically valid, risk management based framework for setting priorities, planning, implementing and reporting on the management of contaminated sites; 4) to remediate, based on approved resource levels, all National Classification System (NCS) Class 1 contaminated sites in the North, and Class 1 and 2 contaminated sites on reserve, on a priority basis, unless it can be demonstrated that for a specific site an alternative form of management is appropriate; 5) to promote the social and economic benefits that may accrue to First Nations, Inuit and northerners when carrying out activities required by this policy; and 6) to promote the federal "polluter pay" principle. CIRNAC intends to establish Standing Offer Agreements (SOA) for multiple qualified Contractors to supply Geotechnical and Hydrotechnical Engineering Services for several abandoned mine sites throughout Yukon, including the following areas subject to Comprehensive Land Claims Agreements (CLCAs): 1. Carcross/Tagish First Nation Final Agreement 2. Champagne and Aishihik First Nation Final Agreement 3. First Nation of Nacho Nyak Dun Final Agreement 4. Kluane First Nation Final Agreement 5. Kwanlin Dün First Nation Final Agreement 6. Little Salmon/Carmacks First Nation Final Agreement 7. Selkirk First Nation Final Agreement 8. Ta'an Kwäch'än Council Final Agreement 9. Teslin Tlingit Council Final Agreement 10. Tr'ondëk Hwëch'in Final Agreement 11. Vuntut Gwitchin First Nation Final Agreement The intent is to award up to five (5) Standing Offer Agreements for a period from Standing Offer Award date to March 31, 2030, with two (2) one (1) year option periods. Level of Security: there are no security requirements applicable to this requirement.

title: Access Control and Intrusion Detection Services
description: The Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) requires the provision of parts and labour (technical support, programming, installation, service, and maintenance) on an “as and when requested” basis for its Integrated Security System (ISS) at CRA locations across Canada. The CRA is considering the conversion of up to 51 sites currently using a combination of Digital Security Controls (DSC) Intrusion Detection Systems and Kantech Access Control systems to a unified Kantech Intrusion/Access Control platform. The site counts identified below represent the CRA’s current intended conversion plans for planning and estimation purposes only and do not constitute a commitment to convert any specific number of sites. The CRA requires the goods and services referenced above in the following regions: 1. National Capital Region (NCR) – up to 11 sites identified for potential conversion; 2. Ontario – up to 13 sites identified for potential conversion; 3. Quebec – up to 1 site identified for potential conversion; 4. Atlantic – up to 4 sites identified for potential conversion; and 5. Western – up to 22 sites identified for potential conversion. Bidders may submit a bid for one (1) or more Regions identified in this RFP. Only one (1) bid submission is required, regardless of the number of Regions for which the Bidder is submitting a bid. The Bidder's submission must clearly identify each Region for which it is proposing to provide the required goods and services. For each Region bid, the Bidder must provide all information required by this RFP, including any Region-specific technical information, resource information, and pricing, in the format prescribed in the bid solicitation documents. Requirement, project experience, certification, corporate qualification, or other bid components that are not Region-specific need only be submitted once and will be evaluated for all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. Bids for Multiple Regions: Requirements identified as Region-specific will be evaluated only for the applicable Region. Requirements that are not Region-specific will be evaluated once and will apply to all Regions included in the Bidder's submission. The CRA will evaluate each Region independently. Where a Bidder fails to meet a Region-specific requirement, the CRA may declare the bid non-responsive for that Region only. For greater certainty, a determination that a bid is non-responsive for one (1) Region will not, in itself, render the Bidder's submission non-responsive for any other Region for which a bid has been submitted, provided all applicable requirements for those Regions are met. The CRA intends to award up to five (5) contracts to fulfill this requirement. A Bidder may be awarded a contract for one (1) Region, multiple Regions, or all five (5) Regions. The period of the resulting contract(s) will be for three (3) firm years. The contract(s) will include four (4) irrevocable one-year options to extend the period of the contract(s). The contract(s) will also include provisions allowing the CRA to add, remove or modify products and sites. A bid must comply with the requirements of the bid solicitation and meet all mandatory evaluation criteria to be declared responsive. For each Region, the responsive bid with the highest combined rating of technical merit and price will be recommended for award of a contract. Each Region will be evaluated separately. Where the same Bidder is ranked first for multiple Regions, the CRA will award a single contract covering the Regions for which that Bidder is the highest-ranked responsive bidder. The Bid Compliance and Remedy Process (BCRP) defined in Part 4.2 will apply. Proposal documents and supporting information must be submitted in either English or French. Questions must be directed in writing to the contracting authority via email: Timothy.Berg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids must be submitted by using the Connect service provided by the Canada Post Corporation. When responding, the proposal MUST be delivered to: Canada Revenue Agency Bid Receiving Unit BRUg@cra-arc.gc.ca Bids will not be accepted if emailed directly to this email address. This email address must be used to request that CRA open a Connect conversation, as detailed in Standard Instructions 2003. Bidders must not use their own licensing agreement for Connect to initiate a Connect conversation with CRA. The CRA reserves the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. There are security requirements associated with this requirement. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. The Federal Contractors Program (FCP) for employment equity applies to this procurement. This bid solicitation 1000536720/B cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 1000536720/A dated 2026-03-27 with a closing of 2026-05-19 02:00 PM EDT. This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. For additional information, consult the bid solicitation document. National Capital Region (NCR) – $100,000 CAD; 2. Ontario – $100,000 CAD; 3. Quebec – $50,000 CAD; 4. Atlantic – $50,000 CAD; and 5. Western – $100,000 CAD.

title: English to Inuktitut Translation Services
description: Limited to firms on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). This solicitation of offer is limited to offerors registered on the Inuit Firm Registry (IFR). Background Pursuant to section 46 of the Nunavut Act, the Auditor General is required to annually audit accounts and financial statements of the Government of Nunavut. As part of this requirement, the Office of the Auditor General of Canada (the OAG) produces a variety of documents, including the annual Nunavut report, that need to be translated from English into Inuktitut, in either the North or South Baffin dialect. Translated documents will also need to be edited and updated. Objective The objective of this procurement process is for the Contractor to provide timely, consistent and reliable English to Inuktitut translation and editing services for Nunavut reports, opening statements and communication products that will be presented by the OAG to the government of Nunavut. The OAG will also require translation or editing of other types of documents varying in length and topic throughout the year, including consolidated financial statements. The Contractor will perform all work from its own facilities. No travel is anticipated for the duration of the resulting contract. In executing the work, Contractor managed devices, tools and IT services will only be used when processing unprotected information. The OAG will provide a laptop computer and access to the OAG network when the work requires access to protected information. Term The period of the Contract is from 1-April-2027 to 31-March-2029 inclusive, with the option to extend the Contract for up to two (2) additional two-year periods.

Trade agreement: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) World Trade Organisation-Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO-AGP) Canada Ukraine Free-Trade Agreement (CUFTA) Canada Korea Trade Agreement (CKTA) Canada free trade agreements with Chile/Colombia/Honduras/Panama Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) Policy on Reciprocal Procurement: This solicitation is open only to Canadian suppliers and to Suppliers of an applicable trading partner. Competitive Procurement Strategy: lowest priced compliant bid. Set-aside under the Procurement Strategy for Indigenous Business: This procurement is not subject to any set-asides for Indigenous Suppliers. Comprehensive Land Claim Agreement: This procurement is not subject to a Comprehensive Land Claims Agreement. Security Requirements: This contract includes security requirements. Nature of Requirements: The following is a summary of the Statement of Work for this requirement. The Correctional Service Canada (CSC), CORCAN in the Atlantic region, is seeking a qualified Contractor to provide professional mechanical services for the repair and maintenance of its equipment in different manufacturing sites in the provinces of New Brunswick and Nova Scotia. Objectives: The Contractor must perform preventative maintenance and repair on tools, machinery and different equipment at various manufacturing sites in the Atlantic Region. Deliverables: The Contractor’s Technical Resource must perform the work at various CSC locations in the Atlantic Region as listed below: Community Industries Moncton – 310 Baig boulevard, Moncton, New Brunswick Dorchester Penitentiary – 4902 Main Street, Dorchester, New Brunswick Springhill Institution – 330 McGee Street, Springhill, Nova Scotia 1. The Contractor must provide the Project Authority: a. A monthly report that includes the following as a minimum: i. the date at which the Contractor performed the work; ii. the Work Site where the work was completed; iii. a brief description of the preventative maintenance and repair services performed, including the tools, machinery, or equipment serviced, and the work completed; iv. The total time spent maintaining and repairing each tool, machinery, equipment. 2. The Technical Resource (technician) must: a. Perform maintenance, repairs, installation and relocation of CORCAN tools, machinery and equipment according to the schedule of tasks to be performed. b. Complete a time sheet and obtain approval from a CORCAN Shop Supervisor on site at the end of each workday or service call. c. Provide the CORCAN official on site with a service report before leaving the site. The service report must identify the tool, machinery, or equipment serviced and document the work performed, findings, test results, parts installed or recommended, any outstanding efficiencies, and the operational status of the asset. The Technical Resource must leave a copy of the service report on site and provide the original to the on-site Production Supervisor, Shop Instructor or Operations Manager upon request. d. Prepare and submit a schedule of planned tasks for the following week to the CORCAN Shop Supervisor each Friday. Any conditions for participation of suppliers not specified in solicitation documentation: none. Estimated quantity of commodity: see solicitation document statement of work and basis of payment. Duration of Contract and Time Frame for Delivery: Period of the Contract: The Work is to be performed during the period of February 1, 2027, to January 31, 2028 with the option to renew for three (3) additional one-year periods. title: Web-based Platform for Whole Building Life Cycle Analysis (WBLCA) and Embodied Carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction
description: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. This procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. The solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. At a minimum, the platform shall enable: - Intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - Import and export capabilities for compatible whole building Life Cycle Assessment (wbLCA) submission reports and raw data; - Dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - The creation of an anonymized public dataset. The Platform MUST comply with Government of Canada security requirements for Protected A information and meet Canadian-based data residency requirements.

title: inversion of the electric field streaming otential-controlled source electromagnetic (spCSEM) data acquired at the Aquistore site
description: The objective of this work is to perform an inversion of the electric field spCSEM data acquired at the Aquistore site. An equivalent point-source SP inversion of the electrical related data should be performed to estimate a) fluid injection intensity (source strength), b) pore pressure gradient around the injection point, c) pressure propagation away from the injector, and d) changes in pressure-driven flow behavior through time. NRCan expects that the contractor uses the calculated pressure gradients to reconstruct plume boundaries (subject to additional information).

title: Logistics Analysis of Damaged, Defective, or Recalled Lithium-Ion and Lithium-Metal Batteries in Canada
description: The primary objective of this study is to collect and analyze data and comprehensively describe the recycling process and logistics for the transportation of DDR lithium-ion and lithium-metal batteries in Canada. This is carried out using Geographic Information Systems (GIS) analytics and mapping along with statistical data analyses and research. The results of this study will provide TC and TDG Regulations with data / information for the purpose of contributing to informed policy decisions regarding safety regulations.

title: Oxygen regulator overhaul kits (ACAN)
description: 1. Advance Contract Award Notice (ACAN) An ACAN is a public notice indicating to the supplier community that a department or agency intends to award a contract for goods, to a pre-identified supplier, thereby allowing other suppliers to signal their interest in bidding, by submitting a statement of capabilities. If no supplier submits a statement of capabilities that meets the requirements set out in the ACAN, on or before the closing date stated in the ACAN, the contracting officer may then proceed with the award to the pre-identified supplier. 2. Definition of Requirement The Department of National Defence (DND) has a requirement for the supply of the following: • Item: Oxygen Regulator Overhaul Kit (Parts Kit, Elastom) • Part Number (PN): 909-010-073 • NATO Stock Number (NSN): 1660-00-385-2846 • NATO Commercial and Government Entity Code (NCAGE): 80477 (Adams Rite Aerospace, Inc.) • Quantity: 120 units The explicit purpose of these flight-safety kits is to execute a critical engineering program to refurbish and recondition the legacy onboard oxygen regulators across the CF188 Hornet fighter aircraft fleet in order to extend their operational service life. 3. Criteria for assessment of the Statement of Capabilities (Minimum Essential Requirements) Any interested supplier must demonstrate by way of a formal Statement of Capabilities that its product meets the following mandatory criteria: • Traceability and Configuration: The supplier must provide certified proof of a direct, unbroken supply chain traceability path to the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), Adams Rite Aerospace, Inc. (NCAGE: 80477), ensuring the component matches Part Number: 909-010-073. OR • Technical Data Equivalence: If an alternative, non-OEM kit is proposed, the supplier must provide a complete engineering data package—including precise chemical compound formulations, material tolerances, and dimensional blueprints—sufficient to undergo a full engineering review by DND’s Technical Airworthiness Authority (TAA) to verify compatibility with the legacy CF188 Hornet oxygen regulator architecture. • Regulatory Airworthiness Certification: The supplier must provide an official Certificate of Conformance or equivalent airworthiness release documentation that satisfies the requirements of the DND’s TAA for critical pilot life-support equipment. 4. This procurement is subject to the following trade agreement(s) • World Trade Organization Agreement on Government Procurement (WTO GPA) - Revised • Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA) • Canada-Honduras Free Trade Agreement • Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA) • Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) • Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) • Canada-Ukraine Free Trade Agreement 2023 Modernized (CUFTA) • Canada-UK Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) • Canada-Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA) • Canada-Colombia Free Trade Agreement • Canada-Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA) 5. Justification for the Pre-Identified Supplier The parts and service sought by the Department of National Defence (as outlined under part 2) are only available from Blue Aerospace LLC as authorized re-seller of the original equipment manufacturer and holder of intellectual property rights, Adams Rite Aerospace, Inc. 6. Government Contracts Regulations Exception The following exception to the Government Contracts Regulations is invoked for this procurement under subsection 6(d) - "only one person is capable of performing the work". 7. Exclusions and/or Limited Tendering Reasons The following exclusion(s) and/or limited tendering reasons are invoked under: Canadian Free Trade Agreement (CFTA), Article 513.1: Limited Tendering (b) (ii) the protection of patents, copyrights, or other exclusive rights; Canada–Chile Free Trade Agreement (CCFTA), Article Kbis-09: Tendering Procedures, para 1 : Limited Tendering b. where the goods or services can be supplied only by a particular supplier and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists; Canada–Colombia Free Trade Agreement (CCoFTA), Article 1409 Limited Tendering b. ii. The protection of patents, copyrights or other exclusive rights; Canada–Honduras Free Trade Agreement (CHFTA), Chapter 17, Article 17.11 Limited Tendering (b) (ii) the good or service is protected by a patent, copyright or other exclusive intellectual property right; Canada–Korea Free Trade Agreement (CKFTA), which defers to WTO-AGP Article XV, Limited Tendering b) when, for works of art or for reasons connected with protection of exclusive rights, such as patents or copyrights; Canada–Panama Free Trade Agreement (CPFTA), Chapter 16, Article 16.10 Limited Tendering b. ii. a good or service being procured is protected by a patent, copyright or another exclusive right; Canada–Peru Free Trade Agreement (CPAFTA), Article 1409: Limited Tendering (b) (ii) the protection of patents, copyrights or other exclusive rights; World Trade Organization – Agreement on Government Procurement - Revised (WTO-AGP), Article XV – Limited Tendering b. Limited Tendering b) when, for works of art or for reasons connected with protection of exclusive rights, such as patents or copyrights, or in the absence of competition for technical reasons, the products or services can be supplied only by a particular supplier and no reasonable alternative or substitute exists; Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), Article 19.12(b)(ii) the protection of patents, copyrights or other exclusive rights; Canada-United Kingdom Trade Continuity Agreement (Canada-UK TCA) - The provisions of CETA are incorporated by reference into and made part of this Agreement; Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP), Article 15.10 (b) (ii) the protection of patents, copyrights or other exclusive rights; Canada–Ukraine Free Trade Agreement - 2023 Modernized (CUFTA) -The provisions of WTO-AGP Article XV, Limited Tendering are incorporated by reference into and made part of this Agreement. 8. Period of the proposed contract or delivery date o Delivery of the items is to begin by 01 March 2027. 10. title: Karstulan koulukuljetusten hankintakonsultointi
description: Karstulan koulukuljetusten hankintakonsultointi Karstulan kunta valmistelee koulukuljetuspalvelujen kilpailuttamista kolmen vuoden sopimuskaudelle sekä kahdelle erilliselle optiovuodelle. Hankinnan kohteena on asiantuntijapalvelu, jossa valittava hankintakonsultti suunnittelee ja toteuttaa koulukuljetusten kilpailutuksen yhteistyössä Karstulan kunnan kanssa. Konsultin tulee huolehtia kilpailutusprosessin lainmukaisesta, tarkoituksenmukaisesta ja aikataulun mukaisesta toteuttamisesta. Tavoitteena on muodostaa koulukuljetuspalveluista toiminnallisesti selkeä ja kilpailukelpoinen hankintakokonaisuus, joka turvaa oppilaiden turvalliset ja toimivat kuljetukset, mahdollistaa keskenään vertailukelpoisten tarjousten antamisen, huomioi Karstulan kunnan alueelliset olosuhteet, edistää toimivien kuljetusmarkkinoiden muodostumista, sisältää selkeän ja hallittavan hinnoittelumallin, mahdollistaa sopimuksen tehokkaan seurannan sopimuskauden aikana sekä vähentää hankintamenettelyyn ja sopimuskauteen liittyviä oikeudellisia ja taloudellisia riskejä. Koulukuljetusten varsinaisen sopimuskauden suunniteltu alkamisajankohta on 1.8.2027. Sopimuskausi on kolme kouluvuotta sekä kaksi erillistä optiovuotta, päättyen näiden jälkeen 31.7.2032. Konsulttipalveluun tulee sisältyä seuraavat tehtäväkokonaisuudet: 1. koulukyytihankinnan ja sen osakokonaisuuksien suunnittelu 2. markkinakartoituksen ja tarvittaessa markkinavuoropuhelun suunnittelu ja toteuttaminen 3. tarjouspyynnön, palvelukuvauksen ja sopimusehtojen laatiminen 4. vertailuperusteiden, pisteytysmallin ja hinnoittelurakenteen muodostaminen 5. hankintailmoituksen ja tarjouspyynnön julkaiseminen HILMAssa 6. tarjoajien kysymyksiin annettavien vastausten valmistelu 7. tarjousten tarjouspyynnönmukaisuuden tarkastaminen 8. tarjousten vertailu ja vertailuasiakirjojen laatiminen 9. hankintapäätösesityksen valmistelu perusteluineen 10. hankintaoikaisujen, oikaisuvaatimusten ja muiden muutoksenhakutilanteiden käsittelyyn osallistuminen 11. sopimusasiakirjojen valmistelu ja sopimusten viimeistely. Koulukyytikilpailutuksessa laadittavan tarjouspyynnön tulee olla kirjallinen ja niin selkeä, että sen perusteella voidaan antaa keskenään vertailukelpoisia tarjouksia. Hankinnan kuvaus, soveltuvuusvaatimukset, vertailuperusteet, tarjousten määräaika ja voimassaolo ovat tarjouspyynnön keskeisiä tietoja.,

Hankinnan sisältö, vaatimukset ja ehdot on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteissä.,

Hankinnan kuvaus, soveltuvuusvaatimukset, vertailuperusteet, tarjousten määräaika ja voimassaolo ovat tarjouspyynnön keskeisiä tietoja.,

title: Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet
description: Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet Kittilän lukion peruskorjauksen yhteydessä uusitaan osa irtokalusteista. Kittilän kunta pyytää tarjouksia Kittilän lukion uusittavista irtokalusteista tämän tarjouspyynnön ja sen liitteiden mukaisesti. Kittilän lukion irtokalusteet kilpailutetaan käänteisenä kilpailutuksena eli ns. ranskalaisena urakkana. Tarjoukset annetaan kalustuksesta sekä suunnitteluprosessista. Valittavalle toimittajalle kuuluu irtokalustuksen kokonaissuunnittelu yhdessä tilaajatahon kanssa sekä kalusteiden toimittaminen laadittuja suunnitelmia noudattaen. Tilaaja valitsee tarjouksista laadullisilta ominaisuuksiltaan parhaan vaihtoehdon. Tarjoukset arvioidaan kokonaisuutena ja arviot perustellaan sanallisesti. Koko hankinnan (suunnitteluprosessi, kalusteet, kalusteiden toimitus-, kokoamis- ja asennuspalvelut sekä pakkausmateriaalien poiskuljetus) kokonaishinta on 165 000 € (alv 0 %). Tilaajalla on oikeus kasvattaa tai supistaa valitun toimittajan kanssa käytyjen neuvottelujen pohjalta hankinnan kokonaishintaa +/- 10 %. Tarjouspyynnössä ja sen liitteissä on kuvattu tarkemmin hankinnan kohde sekä tarjoukseen sisällytettävät liitteet. Hankinnan toteuttajaksi valitaan yksi toimittaja.,

title: Intrinsic Market Resilience (IMR)
description: The evolution of markets from physical trading floors to interconnected, electronic venues has introduced new speed, transparency, and efficiency, but has also created new attack surfaces and systemic risks. Modern markets, which host trading for everything from equities and bonds to energy and cloud computing resources, can be manipulated in ways unanticipated by their designers. The 2010 United States Equity market "flash crash" and the 2000-2001 California energy crisis demonstrated how weaknesses in a market's public interfaces could have dramatic consequences. Similar design issues in today's complex, interacting market systems could be used to cause economic damage, which the IMR program technology seeks to prevent. The IMR program aims to develop repair methods to protect essential economic sectors against devastating attacks that exploit the public interfaces of modern markets. Current legal and regulatory protections focus on deterring profit-seeking manipulation and ensuring compliance, but they do not sufficiently protect markets from adversaries aiming simply to cause disruption. The IMR program seeks to address this gap by developing the tools to automatically model market designs, identify hidden weaknesses, and recommend and analyze repairs on the market models to make markets fundamentally more resilient to attack. IMR aims to combine Large Language Model (LLM)-based automation with rigorous modeling and analysis to identify remediations for market weaknesses. The program will develop formal notations to precisely describe how markets operate and coordinate, creating machine-analyzable models from informal descriptions like regulatory filings and technical specifications. Against these models, IMR will formulate and assess "resilience conjectures� - mathematical statements about desirable market properties, such as the inability for actors to manipulate prices without risking loss. By automatically analyzing these conjectures, the program aims to prove that a market design is resilient in specific ways or, if it is not, to generate a counterexample that illustrates a concrete weakness. These counterexamples will then be used to refine the conjectures and, ultimately, to recommend and confirm specific repairs to the market's design. This approach is intended to provide a capability to protect U.S. markets against adversaries who wish to cause chaos, ensuring the stability of both civilian and military critical resources that rely on modern market mechanisms.

Elle concerne les établissements parties suivants : CH de Valence, Groupement hospitalier Portes de Provence, Hôpitaux Drôme Nord, CH d'Ardèche Méridionale, CH Drôme Vivarais, CH Privas Ardèche, CH Crest, CH Villeneuve de Berg, CH Intercommunal Vercors Isère, CH Die, CH Cévennes Ardéchoises, CH Tournon, CH Bourg-Saint-Andéol-Viviers, CH Lamastre, CH Nyons, CH Buis-les-Baronnies, CH Le Cheylard, CH Vallon Pont d'Arc, GCS BIH), GCS RND) --- Contexte de la procédure : Afin de disposer d'une capacité de fourniture performante, la Fonction Achat Mutualisé du GHT Drome Ardèche a décidé d'utiliser la technique d'achat des &quot;systèmes d'acquisition dynamique&quot; (SAD) pour répondre à ses besoins ponctuels et spécifiques. L'objectif est de répondre au juste besoin des établissements dans des délais de livraison raisonnable, sans rupture d'approvisionnement. --- Forme du contrat : Le marché est un marché de fournitures passé selon la technique d'achat du système d'acquisition dynamique au sens du 4° de l'article L2125-1 du Code de la commande publique. Il est soumis aux dispositions des articles R.2162-37 à R.2162-51 du code de la commande publique. La procédure est entièrement électronique, dès la publication de l'avis de mise en oeuvre du système jusqu'à son expiration. Par nature, le système d'acquisition dynamique est multi-attributaire. Les modalités de remise en concurrence et d'exécution des marchés spécifiques sont prévues à l'article « Marchés spécifiques » du CCAP. Conformément à l'article R2162-41 du code de la commande publique, l'acheteur offre par voie électronique, pendant toute la durée de validité du système, un accès libre, direct et complet aux documents de la consultation. En application de l'article R2162-43 du même code, tout opérateur économique peut demander à participer au système d'acquisition dynamique pendant sa durée de validité

title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source IDIQ contract to Airborne Systems North America, Inc for MMPC Training Services
description: The purpose of this special notice is to provide the Government�s intent to issue a sole source Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract to Airborne Systems North America, Inc. (CAGE 57172), 5800 Magnolia Ave, Pennsauken, New Jersey 08109 for Multi-Mission Parachute Course (MMPC) training services. These services include providing continuous Military Free Fall (MFF) and parachuting training for non-MFF qualified Marines using the designated United States Marine Corps Parachute System-2 (PS-2), in accordance with the approved United States Army Special Operations Command certified MMPC Program of Instruction. Course instruction will ensure successful graduates are qualified to employ the PS-2 during Marine Corps airborne operations. A sole source award will be made on the basis of other than full and open competition under the authority of 10 U.S.C. � 3204(a)(1), as implemented by FAR 6.103-1(b), Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services Will Satisfy Agency Requirements. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code assigned is 611699, All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction, with a size standard of $16.5 million. This IDIQ contract will have an ordering period of five (5) years, from 31 March 2027 through 30 March 2032, and will include FAR Clause 52.217-8 with an option to extend the contract for up to six (6) additional months of service. The contract will contain Firm Fixed Price (FFP) line items for years 1 through 5, with an estimated quantity of nine (9) sessions per year and forty-five (45) sessions total. Additionally, the contract will offer a FFP line item for the FAR 52.217-8 option extension, consisting of an estimated four (4) additional sessions. Under these line items, the Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, materials, and facilities to conduct the course in accordance with the Performance Work Statement. The anticipated award date is 31 March 2027. This is not a request for competitive quotes. The Government is not seeking responses to this special notice. The determination not to compete this contract action is solely within the discretion of the Government. Responses shall be submitted in writing and emailed to the Contract Specialist, Jesse T. Wise at jesse.t.wise.mil@usmc.mil, or the Contracting Officer, Christa Eggleston-Scott at christa.eggleston-sc@usmc.mil.

title: GSA OASIS 8(a) - RISK MANAGEMENT AND INTERNAL CONTROL PROGRAM/INTEGRATED RISK MANAGEMENT SUPPORT SERVICES for US FLEET FORCES COMMAND
description: The U.S. Fleet Forces Command (USFFC) Risk Management and Internal Control program (RMIC) and Integrated Risk Management (IRM) assistant position maintains compliance with the Federal Managers� Financial Integrity Act (FMFIA) Public Law 97-255; Office of Budget and Management (OMB) Circular A-123; U.S. Government Office of Accountability (GAO) Standards for Internal Control in the Federal Government; Department of Defense Statement of Assurance Execution Handbook; Department of Defense Instruction (DoDI) 5010.40, DoD Enterprise Risk Management and Risk Management and Internal Control Program; Department of the Navy Integrated Risk Management Program Handbook; and OPNAV Instruction 5200.25, Risk Management and Internal Controls Program. This includes all matters of importance to the Navy and Commander, USFFC, with particular emphasis on advising and coordinating with stakeholders responsible for executing the principles of fraud risk assessment; entity-level controls evaluation; risk evaluation and management; and internal control evaluation.

Army Contracting Command, Redstone Arsenal (ACC-RSA) is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) pursuant to Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul 15.101(c) solely for information and planning purposes. This notice may be cross posted on other official U.S. Government websites. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the United States Government to contract for any supply or service whatsoever. All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary; the United States Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the United States Government. Responses will be treated as information only and not as a proposal. The information herein is subject to change and in no way binds the Government to pursue any course of action. ACC-RSA is conducting market research on behalf of US Army Transformation and Training Command (T2COM), Combat Capabilities Development Command Aviation and Missile Center (DEVCOM AvMC) to ascertain the capabilities of interested parties in outfitting US Government buildings and/or facilities for Redstone Arsenal, Alabama. title: Y1DA--NRM-CONST 528-CSI-102 Urology Equipment Site Prep | FY27 NRM
description: The purpose of this project is to renovate two Cystoscopy rooms (214 and 215), Procedure Room (212), Procedure Room (211), Check-In area, Office, Control, Vestibule, Dressing, Toilet and Corridor. The two Cystoscopy rooms (214 and 215) will also receive new medical equipment. The Buffalo VAMC requires a Contractor to perform construction work necessary to accomplish this goal. The anticipated Construction Period of Performance is estimated to be 720 days. This effort intends to perform site preparation renovations to support the installation of new medical equipment. The Contractor shall prepare rooms 214 and 215 to receive new equipment. A control room (215-1) is included and an electrical room (214-1) with new electrical panels and equipment is included in the design. In addition, Procedure Rooms 212 and 211, a stretch alcove, a check-in area, office, dressing area and restroom are included in this scope of work

title: Z1DA--528A8-22-814 Consolidate Primary Care Reception
description: This procurement is for construction services for second part of the Consolidate Primary Care (CPC) projects phase 1 that will continue to consolidate the primary care units currently located on the 1st, 4th, and 8th floors in Building 1 of the Albany VA Medical Center located at 113 Holland Avenue, Albany NY 12208. The three primary care units are being combined on the first-floor core of the Albany VA Medical Center. In this phase, a new reception area shall be built to accommodate six (6) Medical Support Assistants (MSA) desks and a waiting lobby. This project also includes the relocation of the Agent Cashiers office in the existing space. The overall project footprint is approximately 5,000 sqft. The project consists of a phased construction approach, which includes restrictions on when certain construction activities can be performed. The contractor is required to follow all VA safety and infection prevention requirements at all times

title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 under the Attachments for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 under the Attachments. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period? Event Date: Monday, 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST Event Location: 2401 SE Monterey Rd, Stuart, FL 34996 *Everyone will need to have a driver's license or id to get through security. All responses under this Special Notice shall be sent via email to Nicole Batista-Cruz at Nicole.M.Batista-Cruz@usace.army.mil, and Ruth Rodriguez at ruth.c.rodriguez@usace.army.mill. Your email subject line should be addressed as "St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day Registration (Company Name) - W912EP-27-Z-1CUE " to ensure the request is handled in a timely manner. title: Pre-Solicitation Notice - Clinical East Staffing IDIQ
description: The purpose of this synopsis is to provide notification of the proposed contract action under solicitation number: RFP 7571MN27R00011 for the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), Program Support Center (PSC), Federal Occupational Health (FOH) Clinical East Staffing Services. The Government intends to release the solicitation in 1st Quarter Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 through the System of Award Management (SAM.gov) as a Small Business set-aside. The purpose of this requirement is to secure continuing services for occupational health professionals to support Federal Occupational Health (FOH), a component within the Program Support Center (PSC) under the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). FOH defines Occupational Health Services (OHS) as the seamless coordination of comprehensive services using a data-driven approach to assist agencies in achieving a culture of health and high performance. FOH services are designed to improve health outcomes and employee productivity, while reducing occupational health risks, absenteeism, and overall employee health care costs. title: Q702--St. Louis JC Bed Tower IOTA IDIQ
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 6, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition and Activation (IOTA) Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal IOTA Services for the St. Louis John Cochran Veterans Affairs Medical Center, New Bed Tower. This requirement supports VA's mission by providing contractor services to help support the activation. The intended contract type is an Indefinite Delivery Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) with an eight (8) year ordering period. The VA St. Louis Health Care System - John Cochran Division (VA STLHCS-JC), located at 915 North Grand Boulevard, St. Louis, Missouri, is part of a two-division health care system that also includes the Jefferson Barracks VAMC approximately 18 miles south of the John Cochran campus. These facilities serve Veterans in metropolitan St. Louis, Missouri, southwestern Illinois, and the broader Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 15 service area. The John Cochran campus is in a highly constrained urban setting in midtown St. Louis. The existing hospital infrastructure includes Building 1, constructed in 1953, and the Clinical Addition constructed in the mid-1980s. The campus requires modernization to address functional adjacency, physical security/force protection, aging infrastructure, seismic compliance, parking, and clinical capacity concerns. The Department of Veterans Affairs Office of Construction and Facilities Management (CFM), VA St. Louis Health Care System, and the Kansas City District (NWK) U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) are partnering to provide new and replacement facilities for the John Cochran Division. The John Cochran Major Project will relocate inpatient functions to a new seismically compliant Bed Tower, add new functionality, improve departmental adjacencies, replace aging utility infrastructure, and address physical security requirements. The John Cochran Major Project includes campus-wide expansion. Planned new facilities include, but are not limited to, parking garages, a Central Utility Plant, the Bed Tower, an Engineering/Administration building, a motor pool building, and supporting structures. The project includes more than 700,000 net usable square feet of new space. Clinical and administrative services anticipated to be supported include surgery, radiology, pharmacy, surgical services, spinal cord injury inpatient and rehabilitation services, emergency services, engineering, police, nutrition and food services, dialysis, and additional services as refined by the Government-approved program and design documents. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 29 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 7 December 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. The first Task Order (TO#1 Project Management and Pre-Planning Support) will be included as part of the solicitation and awarded concurrently with the IDIQ. Quotes will be required for both the IDIQ and Task Order #1. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for quotes. P.O.C: Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: St. Lucie South Jetty Repair Industry Day
description: This announcement constitutes a Special Notice. This announcement seeks information from industry and will only be used for preliminary planning purposes. THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS AND NO CONTRACT SHALL BE AWARDED FROM THIS SPECIAL NOTICE. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is a SAVE-THE-DATE special notice for an industry day event on 07 December 2026 at 10:00 AM EST. All interested Offerors are required to access SAM.gov for future updates. Please view registration information and details below. The presentation slides and list of attendees will be made available and posted to the subject special notice on SAM.gov after the conclusion of the event. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Jacksonville District will be holding an Industry Day event to gauge the interest, capabilities, and qualifications of various members of the Construction Community, to include Small Businesses. This event will provide information and obtain feedback from interested Offerors prior to issuance of the official solicitation. This requirement is for fiscal year (FY) 2027 award. NAICS Code 237990: Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction Small Business Standard: $45 million Price Target Range: $25 - $50 million Estimated Period of Performance: 730 calendar days Project Background Project Title: St. Lucie South Jetty Rehabilitation Interagency, Martin County, Florida. Project Description: The work consists of rehabilitation of the head structure of the South Jetty at St. Lucie Inlet. This includes a rebuilt rounded head structure and head-to-trunk transition with a marine mattress foundation and toe protection stones. Rehabilitation will require substantial moving and manipulation of both new and existing stones to obtain the required interlocking. The reworking of existing stones is only for incorporation of new stone. The retrieval of existing stone outside of the design template will not be required and is not part of the necessary rework of existing stone. The originally constructed South Jetty is approximately 1,320 feet in length with a crest height of 5.5 feet NAVD88. The crest width is 10 feet and the north and south slopes of the structure slope at 1V:2H. There is an asphalt walkway approximately 1,090 feet in length that runs along the existing jetty crest, terminating eastward at approximately Station 12+00 as shown on the approved permit drawings. Manipulation of stone along the crest may be necessary while completing the required work along the side slopes. The asphalt walkway will need to be removed within the repair area as necessary as work progresses. Any asphalt sections removed, or damaged such that they need to be removed, must be transported and properly disposed of off-site, and will not need to be replaced. Project Information Scope of Work: The proposed work includes rehabilitation of the head of the south jetty structure (the seaward-most 400 to 500 feet) by restabilizing the structure foundation and placing a second layer of large armor stone. The proposed scope includes: Excavating the existing bed material to place a widened marine mattress foundation, expanding the current structure footprint up to 85 feet on the jetty centerline as shown on the approved permit drawings; Placing 9- to 15-ton toe protection stones to form the structure foundation and provide scour protection; Removing and disposing of the remaining asphalt walkway and other debris off-site; Repairing the existing core and reworking the single layer of armor stone, as needed; and, Placing a second layer of 9- to 15-ton armor stone to stabilize the structure. Overview of Construction Staging and Access Requirements: Clearing of access routes and staging areas may be required. Any areas that are disturbed during construction are to be restored to pre-construction conditions or better once jetty rehabilitation work is completed. Expansion and/or improvements of access routes may be required. Maximum limits of access routes and staging areas are shown on the approved permit drawings. Additional Environmental Considerations: Construction will be permitted all year round and confined to daylight hours only. Construction that occurs during turtle and shorebird nesting seasons or has the potential to impact other Endangered Species Act (ESA) Protected Species, is subject to environmental restrictions and monitoring requirements. Refer to Table 1 below for a list of protected species. Access from the water is allowed, but material cannot be dredged outside of the construction limits. All material excavated must pass through a 2-inch screen prior to use as backfill around the jetty structure or on the beach. All screened material must be disposed of off site. Excavated material may be used to build up the east staging area within the limits shown on the approved permit drawings. After jetty rehabilitation work is complete, the staging area must be graded to the beach fill template and native vegetation restored as shown on the approved permit drawings. Requests for Information: Industry is asked to consider the following questions and provide input at the Industry Day: Company/Contractor name, address, point of contact, phone number and e-mail address. Does the Contractor plan to submit a proposal for this contract? Describe the proposed construction methods and equipment needed to rehabilitate the jetty. Address, at a minimum, excavation of existing grade, maintaining open excavation areas, debris removal, and installation of marine mattresses and armor stone. Would temporary earth-retention or water-control measures, such as a cofferdam or similar system, be required to complete the work? Would dewatering be completed if this is the proposed construction methodology? If a cofferdam or other earth-retention system that also excludes all swimming ESA-listed species is not proposed, describe the measures that would be used to prevent the swimming ESA-listed species from entering the active work area during construction, including proposed turtle deterrent measures. ESA-listed species present in the area are included in Table 1 above. Describe the turbidity control measures that would be incorporated into the proposed construction methodology. If it is not feasible, describe the limitation or restrictions for why not. What safety constraints or hazards could limit the practicality of potential construction methods? What temporary protections or operational measures would be needed to perform the work during winter months, given the inlet�s elevated coastal conditions during that period?
